title: ERA5 2 m air over the equatorial Indo-Pacific warms 0.05-0.08 C per decade faster than 114 moored buoys in 2001-2022 while ERA5 SST does not; ERA5 global mean changes by 0.01-0.02 C
abstract: Question: campaign work found input steps in the SST products that are the lower boundary of reanalyses. Is the ERA5 marine 2 m air temperature (T2m), a large part of the ERA5 global mean used for 1.5 C monitoring, consistent with independent in situ air temperature? Approach: we compared ERA5 monthly T2m and SST (1979-2022, NCAR GDEX) with 114 GTMBA moorings (TAO/TRITON, RAMA, PIRATA; air at about 3 m and 1-m SST), 33 NOAA NDBC offshore buoys (14-57 N) and CLASSnmat 2.1.0.2 ship night marine air temperature. We used station-by-month fixed-effect panels, AR(1)-adjusted trend errors and a Nino 3.4 regression. Results: ERA5 T2m minus mooring air temperature has a 2001-2022 trend of +0.079 +/- 0.012 C per decade (ENSO removed +0.049 +/- 0.006; 43 fixed long-record stations +0.107 and +0.063). ERA5 SST minus mooring SST has -0.017 +/- 0.007. The buoy air-sea difference is stable (+0.004; ENSO removed +0.003 +/- 0.007), but the ERA5 air-sea difference at the same months rises (+0.085; ENSO removed +0.039 +/- 0.006). Ships at 20S-20N give +0.073 +/- 0.010. The drift is largest at TAO/TRITON and RAMA, small at PIRATA, and absent at NDBC buoys at 14-25 N; station trends follow the ERA5 air-sea trend map (Spearman 0.27, p = 0.008). ERA5 marine air also responds too weakly to ENSO (-0.068 K per K of Nino 3.4 against buoys). In 10S-10N, ERA5 ocean T2m warms 0.134 C per decade but ERA5 SST only 0.067. Removing the drift at 10S-10N lowers the ERA5 2001-2022 global T2m trend from 0.225 to 0.214-0.218 C per decade and the 2024 value from 1.60 to 1.59 C above 1850-1900 (20S-20N upper bound: 0.204-0.212 and 1.58 C). Limitations: the cause is not identified; extratropical references disagree in sign (ships +0.04 to +0.12, NDBC -0.06), so the extratropics are unresolved and ship NMAT may have its own post-2009 cooling error; mooring sensor changes are not modelled; ERA5 gridded data end in 2022, so 2023-2025 values are extrapolations.
